protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: in_s3 obtains the S3 object body and materializes extractor output before parsing. At the fix parent, GzipExtractor appends each unbounded gz.read result and joins all members; the command extractors use Open3.capture2 and return complete decompressed stdout. An authorized bucket writer can therefore submit a small compressed object whose expansion exhausts Fluentd memory.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: PASS: de1ffbe1e6b9da6f4e09ddddd5cb94eb24239636 is the smallest surviving public first-write of the exploitable default gzip path: it creates in_s3.rb, defaults store_as to gzip, passes the S3 body to @extractor.extract, and implements GzipExtractor with an unbounded gz.read. git log -L independently traces the original extract method to this commit; c6acfac8d1efac1ff10f800fefc11d3c4c4faffd only rewrites it for concatenated gzip members while retaining unbounded gz.read. The later command-extractor commit 3208b05088af166ecd67f0827d8106a0240969c4 adds further affected formats but does not precede the already exploitable gzip origin.
